newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices end lower on buyer reserve.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices end lower on buyer reserve.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower in listless trading due to reserve of buyers, dealers said.
"There are a lot of sellers in the market but no buyers," said one local dealer. "We are still waiting for fresh inquiries after the year-end holidays."
Dealers said in the absence of new factors, local prices were pulled down by the softness in regional markets.
They added that with supply returning to normal due to improving weather, prices were likely to come off further.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 311.50 cents ($1.25) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down 2.50 cents from Monday. February SMR 20 buyer was down two cents at 307.50 cents ($1.23) a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 308 cents a kg, SMR CV at 370, SMR L at 348, SMR 5 at 322, SMR 10 at 309 and drum latex FOB at 240.
The INRO five-day moving average was 241.81 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 6 against 241.91 on Jan 3. The daily indicator price was 241.04 versus 242.09.
